c04.why: Every tight player has lived this exact night, and the single sentence ends on the sting, so the stranger stays to find out why nobody paid him.

c07.why: It names the bad beat the viewer is still angry about and then flatly refuses him the conclusion he drew from it, all in one sentence.

c25.why: Any player recognises himself in one of the two years and smiles at the other, which is the then-versus-now arc people tag a friend under.

c24.why: Everyone can picture the nit at their own table, and the line says his slow leak has a cause the viewer hasn't counted.

c11.why: It turns a thing players boast about into evidence of inexperience, a dare that lands in a single sentence.

c09.why: It opens on a hand the viewer has lost and voices the suspicion he already holds, leaving the reel to say whether it's true.

c19.why: The scene of queens winning only the blinds is familiar, and 'they knew before you raised' makes the viewer want to know what gave him away.

c12.why: It starts with the viewer's own complaint in his own words and answers it at once with a figure that contradicts him.

c14.why: The number comes first, but the turn from discipline to a bill puts a price on a habit tight players are proud of.

c18.why: It opens on the viewer's complaint and ends on an accusation about his memory, though the figure in the middle slows it.
